trajectory.patch:
The kernel panic occurs in `lib/heap/heap.c` at line 380 with the assertion `CHECK(bi < bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk))`.

This assertion is located within the `alloc_chunk` function, which is responsible for finding a suitable free chunk for an allocation request.
The variable `bi` is the bucket index calculated for the requested chunk size (`sz`).
The `bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk)` represents the maximum possible bucket index for a chunk that can fit within the heap (i.e., a chunk of size `h->end_chunk`, which is the total size of the heap in chunk units).

In `sys_heap_init`, the `h->buckets` flexible array member is allocated with `nb_buckets` elements, where `nb_buckets` is calculated as `bucket_idx(h, heap_sz) + 1`. Since `heap_sz` is assigned to `h->end_chunk`, this means the `h->buckets` array has `bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk) + 1` elements. This allows for valid indices from `0` up to `bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk)`.

The original assertion `CHECK(bi < bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk))` incorrectly restricts `bi` to be strictly less than the maximum valid index. If an allocation requests a chunk size that corresponds exactly to the maximum bucket index (`bi == bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk)`), the assertion fails, even though `h->buckets[bi]` would be a valid memory access.

The fix is to change the assertion to allow `bi` to be equal to `bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk)`, thus correcting the off-by-one error in the bucket index validation.

lib/heap/heap.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
	CHECK(bi < bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk));
========
	CHECK(bi <= bucket_idx(h, h->end_chunk));
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
